title: Likelihood Hacking in Probabilistic Program Synthesis
abstract: arXiv:2603.24126v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When language models are trained by reinforcement learning (RL) to write probabilistic programs, they can artificially inflate their marginal-likelihood reward by producing programs whose data distribution fails to normalise instead of fitting the data better. We call this failure likelihood hacking (LH). We formalise LH in a core probabilistic programming language (PPL) and give sufficient syntactic conditions for its prevention, proving that a safe language fragment $\mathcal{L}_{\text{safe}}$ satisfying these conditions cannot produce likelihood-hacking programs. Empirically, we show that GRPO-trained models generating PyMC code discover LH exploits within the first few training steps, driving violation rates well above the untrained-model baseline. translated_title: 概率程序合成中的似然黑客攻击
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.24126v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：当语言模型通过强化学习（RL）训练来编写概率程序时，它们可以通过生成数据分布无法归一化的程序来人为地夸大其边际似然奖励，而不是更好地拟合数据。我们将这种失败称为似然黑客攻击（LH）。我们在一个核心概率编程语言（PPL）中形式化了LH，并给出了其预防的充分语法条件，证明满足这些条件的安全语言片段$\mathcal{L}_{\text{safe}}$无法产生似然黑客程序。实证上，我们展示了GRPO训练的生成PyMC代码的模型在最初的几个训练步骤内就发现了LH漏洞，使违规率远高于未训练模型的基线。我们将$\mathcal{L}_{\text{safe}}$的条件实现为$\texttt{SafeStan}$，一种抗LH的Stan修改版本，并实证表明它在优化压力下抑制了LH。
tldr: 本文首次形式化了概率程序合成中的似然黑客攻击问题，提出了一种安全语言片段及其充分语法条件，并实现为SafeStan以有效抑制强化学习训练中的此类漏洞。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes likelihood hacking in probabilistic program synthesis, proposes a safe language fragment with sufficient syntactic conditions, and implements it as SafeStan to effectively suppress such exploits under RL training.
